articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
• Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.summary: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.keyPoints:
• The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
• Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.
• The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: States need help to rebuild public infrastructure after damage in cyclones

Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured

The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: Cyberabad Police explore one-way traffic system across Biodiversity, HITEC City corridors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyberabad Police have initiated steps to explore a one-way traffic system along the Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace and HITEC City corridor to ease congestion during peak hours.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh, accompanied by Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh, RTC officials and other traffic police personnel, inspected the proposed route on Friday. The inspection covered Biodiversity Junction, IKEA, T-Works, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and surrounding areas.

The proposed one-way corridor would cover Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City Road, Qualcomm and Dallas Centre Road. Officials examined traffic flow patterns, road conditions and major conflict points along the stretch to assess the feasibility of the proposal and identify measures to reduce congestion.

During the inspection, Mr Ramesh instructed officials to prepare a detailed report covering a comprehensive traffic flow study, identified bottlenecks and conflict points, supported by relevant visuals.

He also directed them to conduct a block-wise assessment of buildings contributing to traffic congestion, including the anticipated traffic impact, vehicle volume generated by each building, availability of parking facilities and parking capacity.
The exercise aims to identify suitable traffic management measures and streamline vehicular movement around T-Hub, IKEA, Knowledge City, Qualcomm and Biodiversity.

articles.title: Greater flamingos sighted for the first time at Kere Bhosga

A major highlight was the sighting of greater flamingos at Bhosga Kere for the first time.

A bird walk on this occasion was organised by local group Winged Endeavours as part of the first State-wide initiative under the eBird platform; the exercise aimed to document Karnataka’s bird diversity, recording 62 species across the city during the birding session.
Painted storks sighted at the S.B. lake during the bird count event in Kalaburagi. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

K.S. Aishwarya of Winged Endeavours led the participants of the bird walk across different locations, including lakes and birding hot spots in the city, introducing them to birdwatching and encouraging them to document local birdlife.
Among the species recorded were the purple heron, river tern and Eurasian spoonbill. Migratory visitors included the greater flamingo, common sandpiper, northern shoveler and rosy starling.

Explaining bird migration patterns, Ms. Aishwarya said the movement was driven primarily by a lack of food availability. Depletion of food resources in their native habitats prompted birds to move to regions offering better feeding opportunities. Some destinations also served as breeding grounds, improving the survival prospects of their young, she said.

Kalaburagi’s relatively mild winters make it a suitable seasonal habitat for migratory birds escaping severe cold in their native ranges. Winter visitors are generally spotted in the region from October to early March, she added.

The northern shoveler migrates from Russia, Siberia, Europe and Central Asia, while the common sandpiper arrives from Europe and northern Asia. Greater flamingos visit from parts of Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, and the Middle East. Rosy starlings arrive from Eastern Europe and Central Asia, attracted by grain crops and insects.

Systematic documentation helps understand their seasonal movements and distribution, they said. The observations uploaded to eBird provide useful data for researchers and conservationists studying bird diversity and migration patterns.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s after The Hindu report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Rajasthan police rescue six minors forced into sex work, five arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police acted after taking cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report in August by The Hindu.

The Rajasthan police has rescued six minor girls of the Banchhada community in Jhalawar district and arrested five people – most of whom were related to the girls – for allegedly pushing them into sex work, officers said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Speaking to The Hindu , Jhalawar Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Kumar said that the girls, aged between 12 and 17, were rescued in raids conducted in the Bhawanimandi area on November 3 and that medical and forensic examinations have confirmed sexual exploitation of five of the girls.
Two of the girls have also tested positive for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).

Mr. Kumar said that the action was taken after the police took cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report by The Hindu , which had in August highlighted the problem of children being forced into the sex trade in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur, Neemuch and Ratlam districts.

The Banchhada community, a de-notified tribe , is mainly spread across various districts of Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region and Rajasthan’s Mewar region. The community has long been infamous for being involved in traditional sex work, often by forcing their daughters into sex work from an early age, with their family members and relatives working as pimps.
As per the Jhalawar police, the community has a significant population in about 5-6 villages in the district.

Mr. Kumar said that an SIT headed by Additional SP Ayush Shrotriya was formed for the operation, after which two officers were sent to localities where the community had a presence to gather digital evidence with the help of spy cameras.

“After verifying the digital evidence and intelligence inputs, raids were conducted in localities of the community with over 100 personnel – including women personnel in civil dress – and six girls were rescued,” the officer said.

Mr. Kumar said that an FIR under Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, and Sections 5, 6, 11, 12 and 17 of the The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has been lodged at Bhawanimandi police station.
He said that a separate SIT under Additional SP Bhagchandra Meena has been formed for further investigation into the case.

The police acted after taking cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report in August by The Hindu.

The Rajasthan police has rescued six minor girls of the Banchhada community in Jhalawar district and arrested five people – most of whom were related to the girls – for allegedly pushing them into sex work, officers said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Speaking to The Hindu , Jhalawar Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Kumar said that the girls, aged between 12 and 17, were rescued in raids conducted in the Bhawanimandi area on November 3 and that medical and forensic examinations have confirmed sexual exploitation of five of the girls.

Two of the girls have also tested positive for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).

Mr. Kumar said that the action was taken after the police took cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report by The Hindu , which had in August highlighted the problem of children being forced into the sex trade in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur, Neemuch and Ratlam districts.

The Banchhada community, a de-notified tribe , is mainly spread across various districts of Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region and Rajasthan’s Mewar region. The community has long been infamous for being involved in traditional sex work, often by forcing their daughters into sex work from an early age, with their family members and relatives working as pimps.

As per the Jhalawar police, the community has a significant population in about 5-6 villages in the district.

Mr. Kumar said that an SIT headed by Additional SP Ayush Shrotriya was formed for the operation, after which two officers were sent to localities where the community had a presence to gather digital evidence with the help of spy cameras.

“After verifying the digital evidence and intelligence inputs, raids were conducted in localities of the community with over 100 personnel – including women personnel in civil dress – and six girls were rescued,” the officer said.

Mr. Kumar said that an FIR under Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, and Sections 5, 6, 11, 12 and 17 of the The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has been lodged at Bhawanimandi police station.

He said that a separate SIT under Additional SP Bhagchandra Meena has been formed for further investigation into the case.

fullParagraphs: Yadgir bandh called by various organisations under the leadership of former Minister Narasimha Naik (Rajugouda) evoked a good response across the Yadgir district headquarters, as well as in Shorapur and Hunsagi taluks, on Friday.

​The agitation was staged to demand the uninterrupted release of water from the Basavasagar reservoir through the Narayanpur Left and Right Bank Canals until the end of November to protect standing crops, including paddy, green chili, and cotton.
​Commercial establishments, markets, and shops voluntarily shut down operations until 3 p.m. in solidarity with the farmers. However, public transport remained largely unaffected.
​Hundreds of farmers gathered near the Tahsildar’s office in Yadgir before marching to the Subhash Chandra Bose Circle, where they staged a demonstration for several hours.

​Addressing the rally, Mr. Naik alleged that despite sufficient water storage in the reservoir, discharges were being routed overnight to neighboring Telangana while local agricultural requirements were overlooked. Rebutting district in-charge Minister Sharan Prakash Patil’s denial of the allegations, Mr. Naik claimed that local farmers possessed video evidence documenting the inter-State water transfer.

​He appealed to Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil to allocate at least 14 tmcft of water to Yadgir district to save standing crops, highlighting that 28 tmcft of water had already been reserved for drinking purposes in Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts.

​Mr. Naik also urged Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar to withdraw cases registered against farmers during previous agitations, offering to have himself booked first instead. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigama Limited enforces its proposed Warabandhi shutdown starting November 12.
​The protest garnered support from multiple farmer associations, pro-Kannada outfits, Dalit organisations, and the local Advocates’ Association.

​A formal memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister was submitted through Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve, who assured the protesters that their demands and grievances would be forwarded to higher authorities promptly.

articles.title: ADNOC inks 10-year LNG supply and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday signed a 10-year sales and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2028, further strengthening its presence in India’s expanding gas market.
The agreement marks ADNOC’s fifth LNG supply deal with an Indian company, following similar arrangements with Bharat Petroleum, Indian Oil Corporation, GAIL and Hindustan Petroleum.
Under the agreement, XRG, ADNOC’s international investment arm, will supply LNG produced outside the Gulf and owned by it through ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform.

Rashid Al Mazrouei, Chief Marketing & Origination Officer (LNG) at ADNOC, said, “It represents the first sale of molecules from XRG’s international portfolio, reinforcing our commitment to delivering reliable, long-term LNG supplies.”

He added, “Through our integrated LNG marketing and trading platform, we are connecting our growing international portfolio with customers in key regions across global markets, while providing India with reliable, flexible and long-term LNG supplies.”

ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform also has supply agreements with Japan’s INPEX and Thailand’s Gulf Group. The platform aims to market 47 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG beyond 2030.
Avantika Singh Aulakh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, said, “Through this partnership, Gujarat Energy and ADNOC are joining forces to fully realize the power of our collaboration.”
Gujarat Energy operates a city gas distribution network spanning 44 districts across six states.

articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: For an economy aspiring to become a developed nation by 2047, the statistical blind spots could translate into costly policy mistakes, misdirected investments and ineffective welfare schemes

India’s statistical requirements have outgrown the conventional survey-based architecture, requiring a more scientific and technological architecture to better capture key performance indicators of economy, even as it should avoid the growing risks of synthetic data.

Seeking to move official data collection beyond periodic surveys and administrative records, the VISTAR or Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research is a major overhaul of India’s official statistical system at the centre and state levels using interoperable datasets, bridging data gaps and generating timely, reliable socioeconomic indicators for evidence-based policymaking.

articles.title: Mines Ministry launches ninth round of auctions, offers 20 critical mineral blocks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Till date, across the eight tranches of mineral block auctions, 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks have been offered, of which 64 blocks have been successfully auctioned.

The Ministry of Mines on Thursday launched the ninth tranche of mineral block auctions, featuring 20 critical and strategic mineral blocks, alongside the third tranche of exploration licence auctions covering 11 blocks.
The latest mineral block auction includes deposits of graphite, glauconite, vanadium, gallium, titanium, rare earth elements (REE), tungsten, potash and halite, among other minerals.

The third round of exploration licence auctions, which grants concessions through competitive bidding for reconnaissance and prospecting activities, covers blocks containing copper, potash, halite, vanadium and associated mineralisation.
Across the first eight tranches of mineral block auctions, the government has offered 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks, of which 64 have been successfully auctioned.
Under the exploration licence regime, 11 blocks offered in the first two tranches have also been successfully auctioned.

articles.title: NPCI says MDR charge has been imposed to save the UPI ecosystem from turning ouroboric
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Zero MDR is no longer sustainable; the magnitude of growth places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system, NCPI tells SC

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has said in the Supreme Court that “zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)” for all Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions was no longer sustainable, as functional costs for the phenomenally expanding digital payment industry in India would burn into the public exchequer.

UPI processed as many as 24.51 billion transactions, cumulatively worth approximately ₹29.82 lakh crore, in the month of August 2026 alone, marking its highest-ever monthly volume. An average of approximately 791 million transactions were processed every single day in that month. In Financial Year 2025-26, UPI processed approximately 241.62 billion transactions worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, the NPCI said.

“The figures illustrate not merely growth, but growth of a magnitude that places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system,” the NPCI, represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, submitted in Court.
The Corporation was responding to a challenge in Court to the government’s decision to introduce an MDR of 0.4% on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

Person to person (P2P) transactions, which account for 70% of total UPI transaction value, would remain completely free irrespective of amount, the NCPI said. There would be no transaction or platform fee or other charge permissible for individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI, it added.

It said person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 would also remain “entirely free of MDR”. “This threshold is calibrated to shield the overwhelming majority of everyday, low-value merchant payments of the kind made by ordinary consumers and small merchants alike,” the NPCI said.
The affidavit assured that the amended MDR framework targeted only higher value commerce without disturbing low-value transactions that drive the mass adoption of UPI.

The MDR charge, which did not exceed 0.4%, would apply to P2M transactions above ₹2000. “Effectively, MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions, and approximately 96% of all P2M will remain unaffected,” the NPCI said.
The NPCI countered the petitioners’ contention that an amended MDR framework should have been introduced only through a new legislation and not just through a notification in September.

The NCPI argued that MDR was not a tax, cess, fee, duty or any other statutory levy imposed by or under a legislative enactment. It was plainly a ‘charge’ collected to recover the huge costs associated with the functioning of the payment system, and was in turn, distributed entirely amongst the participants in the UPI ecosystem.

articles.title: CBG blending at 1.7% in H1; pipeline connectivity key to achieving 3% target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: India has a target of blending 3% CBG into D-PNG and CNG by the end of current fiscal, 4% in 2027-28 and 5% in the subsequent year.

India achieved 1.7% blending of compressed biogas (CBG) with domestic piped natural gas (D-PNG) and vehicular compressed natural gas (CNG) in the first half of the current fiscal, but will need an acceleration in sales during the second half to meet the mandated 3% target, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).
The country has set a blending target of 4% for 2027-28, rising to 5% in the subsequent fiscal.

CBG sales stood at 115.9 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during the April-September period, against combined CNG and D-PNG sales of 6,800 MMSCM. With the combined consumption of the two fuels projected at 13,600 MMSCM for the full fiscal, CBG sales will have to rise to 408 MMSCM to achieve the 3% blending target, requiring an additional 292.1 MMSCM over the first-half volume.
Flagging infrastructure gaps, PNGRB stressed the need to connect CBG plants to gas pipelines to ensure assured offtake and better utilisation of installed capacity.

Of the 210 functional CBG plants in the country, capacity utilisation averages just 44%. More significantly, 247 of the 308 plants under construction currently have no plans for pipeline connectivity.

“A reliable pipeline connection gives CBG plant a buyer every day of the year. Plants with a pipeline, or one being built, use 65-69% of their designed capacity. Better pipeline access means better gas offtake and overall use of every plant,” it said.

Besides expanding pipeline infrastructure, the regulator called on larger entities to establish their own CBG blending targets, increase procurement from independent producers and invest in setting up captive CBG plants.

articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 people, including Rohingya refugees, during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers near the Myanmar border, the military said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
One soldier was killed in the clash on Thursday (November 5, 2026) night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

ISPR said that security forces launched an operation in the hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf, close to the border with Myanmar, after receiving a tip-off that an armed gang of 15 to 16 suspected traffickers had abducted around 120 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis.
"During the exchange of fire, an army soldier, Md. Titash Sheikh, was shot. The bullet struck his left shoulder. He was bleeding profusely," the statement said.
Bangladesh hosts more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, most of whom fled a brutal military crackdown in neighbouring Myanmar in 2017.
Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.
The 2017 Myanmar crackdown, which saw Rohingya villages burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case at the UN's top court in The Hague.

On Thursday (November 5, 2026), Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.
There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.

articles.title: Myanmar to conduct byelections next April
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives

Myanmar will hold byelections next April, the polling commission said on Friday (November 6, 2026), encompassing areas where the pro-military parliament could not previously hold voting due to the country's devastating civil war.
The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives.
Myanmar has been embroiled in civil war since the military ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021.
The junta staged phased elections last December and January, which it touted as a return to democracy following the coup.
But the highly restrictive poll was blocked in areas where rebels seized control in opposition to military rule, rejecting the elections as a charade.
The Union Election Commission said byelections will take place on April 4, 2027 in 39 constituencies of the lower and upper houses of Parliament, according to a statement published by state media.
According to an AFP tally, one-third of those constituencies are places where voting in the previous elections was called off for security reasons.
The scheduled votes are in areas where fighting is still raging, though, including the northern region of Sagaing, central Mandalay region and the western state of Chin.
The remaining two-thirds of constituencies will replace lawmakers who have been compelled by the constitution to vacate their seats after being promoted to senior government roles.
Myanmar's Parliament is dominated by lawmakers from the pro-military Union Solidarity and Development Party, while Suu Kyi's party was dissolved and she remains detained.

articles.title: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatar's Emir
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office

U.S. President Donald Trump has discussed efforts to de-escalate tensions in the West Asia in a telephone call with Qatar's Emir as the region remained on edge over the possibility of renewed U.S. military action against Iran.
The telephone call between Mr. Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office.
The two discussed in particular Qatar's mediation efforts aimed at reaching “a comprehensive agreement that ends the crisis and achieves security and stability in the region.”

Qatar has been mediating between the United States and Iran to end the war. Qatar and other U.S.-allied Gulf Arab countries came under heavy fire from Iran earlier in the U.S.-Iran war and have been anxious to avoid a new escalation that could leave them vulnerable to attacks.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts
Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.
The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

articles.title: Ai+ Smartphone to increase smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The smartphone prices are expected to rise up again by up to 10% post Diwali due to memory crisis, lesser inventories and rupee depreciation against US dollar
Ai+ Smartphone on Friday announced to increase the price of its smartphone portfolio by up to ₹3,000 . The new prices will be effective November 11.
The smartphone prices are expected to rise up again by up to 10% post Diwali due to memory crisis, lesser inventories and rupee depreciation against US dollar.
“With fresh inventory being procured at higher memory and component costs, the company has advanced its planned price revision to reflect the updated cost structure,” the company said.

Ai+ Smartphone, a new homegrown smartphone brand, sold over ten lakh devices during the Q3, 2026. “The decision follows stronger-than-anticipated consumer demand, with sales exceeding initial projections and existing inventory being exhausted ahead of schedule,” it added.
Recently, another Indian smartphone brand, Lava, said to increase its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000 post Diwali.
Overall, Indian smartphone shipments went down to a decade low by 20% during the third quarter due diminishing demand and rising average smartphone price (ASP) of the phones.

articles.title: Indian NGO REACH receives Kochon Prize 2026
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB

Resource group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health (REACH), a not-for-profit organisation working to strengthen the tuberculosis (TB) response in India, has been awarded the Kochon Prize 2026, becoming the first civil society, non-profit organisation from India to receive this prestigious global recognition for its contributions to combating TB, a press release said.

Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB. The 2026 Kochon Prize is shared by REACH, the Centre for Health Solutions, Kenya, and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program. Previous winners from India include L.S. Chauhan (2006), head of the Revised National TB Control Programme, the Indian Council of Medical Research (2017) and Molbio Diagnostics (2024). The award was presented at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting held in Indonesia on November 5, 2026.

“Treat the person, not the disease - our journey with TB communities has been just that. We realised early on that overcoming barriers to care means addressing more than clinical needs - it means recognising social, community, family, mental health and situational challenges. That is the essence of integrated care: seeing the whole person, understanding their realities, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that no one is left behind,” said Nalini Krishnan, chairperson and co-founder, REACH.

“REACH is a remarkable and rare organisation that has been consistently ahead of the curve in terms of public health action, and particularly in the field of TB. A women-led organisation, they genuinely care about the people they’re supporting, beyond the numbers, data and reports to donor. However, they combine this with a robust scientific and technical approach and a shrewd understanding of the public health landscape in the country,” said Soumya Swaminathan, chairperson, M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and former chief scientist, WHO, who nominated REACH for the award.

“This recognition is testimony to the dedication of the community health workers, TB Nanbans and TB Champions who work alongside us, and to the families affected by TB and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) who have placed their trust in us. We are deeply grateful to their unwavering commitment and fortitude, and are energised to do more to help facilitate equitable access to health,” said Ramya Ananthakrishnan, director, REACH.

articles.title: Documentary highlights role of family physicians in strengthening primary healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The documentary is intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system

The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care , screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships, built on trust, familiarity and personal attention, remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy Pitchela, project manager for the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.
Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care , screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships, built on trust, familiarity and personal attention, remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy Pitchela, project manager for the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.

Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

articles.title: Opposition trying to destabilise TVK-led government, says Manickam Tagore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He accuses the Opposition of attempting to create uncertainty and undermining the State’s development
TNCC president Manickam Tagore on Thursday alleged that opposition parties were attempting to destabilise the TVK-led government by approaching its MLAs.

Supporting Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar’s allegation that the DMK and AIADMK were attempting to poach TVK MLAs with the BJP’s support, he said those who had lost power were trying to disturb the government.

Speaking to mediapersons, Mr. Tagore said senior leaders of the DMK, AIADMK, and the BJP had repeatedly questioned the stability of the government. “An honest government has been installed, honest Ministers have been appointed, and the Chief Minister has been delivering a clean administration for the past four months,” he said, adding that the Opposition was attempting to create uncertainty and undermine the State’s development.

On Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh’s allegations about foreign funding for protests in Delhi, Mr. Tagore said he should file a police complaint if he had evidence. “Such baseless claims must stop. As a Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, he should act responsibly. Who is stopping him from going to a police station if he has proof?” he asked.
He also accused the BJP of spreading misinformation to divert attention from allegations of electoral malpractice.

The bodies of three fishermen from Tamil Nadu washed ashore at Kothapatnam coast in Ongole on Thursday while the bodies of two more fishermen were found later in the sea by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) officials at Nizampatnam Port.

Using a Dornier aircraft, the ICG staff in coordination with the personnel of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC), Chennai, launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation to find five more fishermen, who were sailing on the same boat that sank 2 km off the shore.

According to sources, three boats set out from Tamil Nadu for fishing On October 29, 2026. Owing to the impact of Cyclone Murasu, two boats were anchored for safety near Ramayapatnam Port on November 2 (Monday), while the third boat proceeded towards Nizampatnam Port.

The nine fishermen on the third boat departed from Nizampatnam to meet the other two teams in Ramayapatnam on November 3 (Tuesday). Due to a storm at sea and intense winds, their boat drifted towards the coast of Adani Krishnapatnam Port and capsized.

The nine were identified as Pakkirisamu Suriya (driver), Kuppan, Mohan, Rajesh, Murugan, Kuppusamy, Vijayakanth, Aravindh and Narayanan. While Narayanan was from Cuddalore, the remaining all were from Chennai.

Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, who was in Kothapatnam to inspect the voting process for the local body elections, visited the place where the bodies of the fishermen washed ashore. ‘’The identification of the bodies will take place after the family members and officials from Tamil Nadu arrive,’’ he added.
“Further action regarding the transport of the bodies and bringing the capsized boat to the shore will be taken in consultation with the officials from Tamil Nadu,’’ the Collector said.
Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, along with the deceased fishermen's family members, reached the mortuary of RIMS Hospital in Ongole for the identification of the bodies.

Andhra Pradesh Fisheries Commissioner Rama Shankar Naik and District Collector P. Raja Babu accompanied the Tamil Naidu Minister. The family members identified four bodies. He said the bodies would be taken to Tamil Nadu after police investigation and post-mortem examination.
"I extend my gratitude to the Andhra Pradesh government for its cooperation. We hope to recover the remaining bodies soon," Mr. Wilson said.

articles.title: School excursion row: UDF leaders release CCTV footage in support of their claims
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The leadership claimed that the visuals showed the principal and the PTA president entering and leaving the establishment, alleging that a bill of ₹1,100 for alcoholic beverages was settled using the PTA president’s personal ATM card.

The controversy surrounding the recent student study tour conducted by the Meenangadi Government Higher Secondary School saw new developments on Thursday (November 5), with the United Democratic Front (UDF) Meenangadi panchayat committee releasing CCTV footage allegedly showing school Principal, Shivi Krishnan, and the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) president Hijas Ulladan entering a bar.

At a press conference, UDF leaders, led by former Meenangadi panchayat president K.E. Vinayan, presented the footage purportedly retrieved from the bar in Nampally, Hyderabad. The leadership claimed that the visuals showed the principal and the PTA president entering and leaving the establishment, alleging that a bill of ₹1,100 for alcoholic beverages was settled using the PTA president’s personal ATM card.

Following the disclosure, the UDF Meenangadi leadership lodged a formal complaint with the Wayanad District Police Chief and announced plans to approach the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. They alleged that students who spoke in support of the school authorities were subjected to severe cyberbullying, intimidation, and harsh online trials by vloggers and online media outlets.

The row originally erupted after allegations emerged that two responsible school officials had consumed alcohol during a recent study tour to Hyderabad. Responding to the accusations, Principal Shivi Krishnan, who is also a leader of a teachers’ association, had refuted the claims and termed them a targeted political move against him.

Though a subsequent medical examination of the principal revealed no presence of alcohol in his blood and a section of students publicly defended him, the UDF countered that online media and vloggers were influenced to sway public opinion, prompting them to release the CCTV footage to substantiate their allegations.

articles.title: Telangana climate conclave to be special feature of global summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Scientists and experts to deliberate on tackling climate change and drought proofing agriculture
The forthcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit – 2026 will feature a special event, Telangana Climate Conclave.

To be held on December 8, the second day of the global summit, the conclave will witness participation of close to 200 scientists, experts from related fields and farmers. The event is being organised to discuss about agriculture patterns that can withstand droughts, animal husbandry, drinking water security, biodiversity, conversion of waste to wealth and other topics.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wanted an exclusive discussion climate change and challenges posed by El Nino during the global summit. The discussion should result in planning short and long term measures to effectively tackle the problems caused due to climate change as well as a special action plan to handle challenges posed by environmental changes.

The Chief Minister at a meeting with senior officials on Thursday reviewed the status of arrangements being made for the global summit and made several suggestions to the officials concerned. Accordingly, it was decided to appoint a liaison officer for every participant besides ensuring that formalities like registration and issuance of passes be completed on arrival at the airport itself. Participants should be provided with detailed information of the summit proceedings in advance and steps should be taken to ensure that they were not inconvenienced at any point of time.

In addition to liaison officers, security officials should be appointed and elaborate arrangements should be made. Special invites should be sent to companies which evinced interest in investing in the State and officials concerned had been directed to ensure that a comprehensive plan for the successful conduct of the event was finalised by November 15.

Officials informed the Chief Minister that extensive arrangements were being made for the summit, including setting up of additional halls for the exhibitions. Steps had been taken to ensure that programmes related to investments, modern technology, innovations and job opportunities were prioritised besides making arrangements for the success of different exhibitions planned as part of the event.

The Raksha Expo, exclusive defence exhibition, would feature display of latest defence developments, aerospace and cyber security aspects along with drones and robotics. Of the 575 firm that had been invited to attend the summit, 49 had evinced interest to attend the global summit. Special arrangements were being made for animation, visual effects, gaming and related fields and an exclusive pavilion was being set up for start ups. It was decided to invite technological solutions in the fields of agriculture, health, protection of government lands and basic amenities as part of the Telangana Innovation Challenge that was made part of the event. Applications for the challenge would be accepted till November 20.

The Chief Minister wanted special focus on tourism sector as part of the summit while steps should be taken to showcase the measures initiated for education, research and skill development by the State government modelled on “Education to Harvard”.

articles.title: CM directs officials to begin Kaleshwaram barrage restoration works in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Final approvals to be secured by month-end; ₹4,193 crore estimated for repairs and restoration

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), with a target of commencing the works in December.

At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. He also asked Ministers to counter the misleading propaganda that water available at Medigadda. It was also discussed in the Cabinet later.

For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open.

On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste.

While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said.

He said the State would not have faced such difficulties during drought conditions had the previous government constructed a barrage at Tummidihatti and completed the Pranahita project. Water from Pranahita could have been brought to Yellampalli at a lower cost, he observed.

Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and senior officials explained the restoration plan for the three barrages. Proposals estimated at approximately ₹4,193 crore had been prepared for the restoration of the three barrages. Under the proposed arrangement, the construction agencies would bear the cost of rectifying defects, while the government would meet the expenditure on additional works.

articles.title: Uncertainty over Nigeria vote as court bars opposition leader
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The ADC, one of the main opposition parties trying to oust President Bola Tinubu, has been mired in lawsuits around its leadership, which have now ensnared its 2027 nominee

A Nigerian court on Thursday (November 5, 2026) declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), just two months before the country’s elections.

The party, which accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of involvement in the lawsuit, will appeal, its spokesman said — but the ruling creates legal headaches for Abubakar and uncertainty for voters with the January 16 vote around the corner.
The ADC, one of the main opposition parties trying to oust President Bola Tinubu, has been mired in lawsuits around its leadership, which have now ensnared its 2027 nominee.

Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision is “another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming general elections”, ADC spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi said in a statement.
Earlier this year, the federal government backed a separate lawsuit over the ADC’s eligibility to contest the 2027 vote in Africa’s most populous country.
Tinubu spokesman Daniel Bwala told AFP the APC “is not involved at all” in the suit over the party’s leadership that sparked Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision.
Nigerian media reported that the federal high court in Abuja overturned the current leadership of the ADC by David Mark, who has been fighting with Nafiu Bala Gombe leading the party.
In ruling against Mr. Mark, the nomination of Mr. Abubakar — made while he was at the party’s helm — has also been tossed, Nigerian media reported.
The decision was handed down a day after Mr. Abubakar launched his campaign with a rally in Sokoto state. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence,” Mr. Abubakar said in a statement.
He did not address the ruling at a rally in northwestern Kebbi state later that day.
