articles.title: Deepavali with pets: Why pet parents are choosing quieter holiday getaways
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As fireworks unsettle dogs and cats, pet owners are trading noisy city celebrations for countryside retreats, pet hostels and quieter holidays

As Deepavali approaches, pets often become anxious at the sound of firecrackers. Dogs and cats may hide under beds or in dark corners, while some lose interest in playtime, walks and even pee breaks. For pet owners, finding ways to ease their distress is an ongoing challenge. Some who love celebrating Deepavali but cannot bear to see their pets shivering and panting are now choosing quieter destinations to spend the festival.
Frodo from Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Pet parent JP Daisy boards her cat at a hostel in Hyderabad’s Kokapet with soundproof rooms during Deepavali. Watching her usually docile Siamese, Sharpay, run helter-skelter as firecracker noise peaks in the evening makes Daisy anxious. “She is a lightweight cat and usually eats very little. During Deepavali, she stops eating. One of our friends suggested a place to board her. Sharpay is not clingy, so boarding her is easy,” she says.

Pet boarding facilities also see a surge in demand during festivals, and not just from people travelling. With diyas lit in homes, unattended flames can pose a safety risk. At Pet Cafe Hyderabad, a boarding facility and restaurant in Banjara Hills, founder Deven Baheti says regulars book slots weeks, sometimes months, ahead of Deepavali.

“The open space and location make it comfortable for pets. Ours is a quiet locality, with few homes bursting firecrackers. To further drown out the noise, we play calming music, use vet-approved anti-anxiety drops and essential oils, and apply calming sprays to help them relax,” says Deven.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”
A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

articles.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school
The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that the child had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts.

Despite "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis" according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral," and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw the child writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP.

articles.title: Over 4,200 firecracker shops permitted for Diwali in Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Traders are requested to obtain licenses online till the festival day and sell crackers in licensed shops only by following safety precautions, says Fire Services DG Venkata Ramana
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response and Fire Services Department issued temporary licenses for 4,226 firecracker shops in the State for the Diwali festival.

As many as 4,307 traders applied for temporary licenses for selling crackers, of which licenses were issued for 4,226 shops (up to November 6). The highest number of 459 traders applied for licenses online from the East Godavari district, followed by Kakinada (365), Krishna (350), Konaseema (317) and 310 applied for licenses for setting up firecracker shops from the Nellore and Kadapa districts.

Speaking to The Hindu on Friday (November 6, 2026), A.P. State Disaster Response and Fire Services in-charge Director General P. Venkata Ramana said that traders can apply for licenses through Whatsapp No.9441236448. Applicants are requested to call State Fire Control Room No. 9100108101 or 7993987418 for any assistance.
This year, the Fire Services Department has introduced an online system and simplified the process for issuing licenses to firecracker traders in the State, said Mr. Ramana.
People purchase firecrackers at a shop in Bhavani Puram in Vijayawada. | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao

Traders can apply for temporary licenses to Whatsapp No.9441236448. Applicants are requested to submit the name, full address where the cracker shop is proposed to set up, name of district and mandal, nearest fire station and mobile number.

Later, the trader will get a Whatsapp message in which a payment link will be given. The applicant should pay ₹500 through QR Code or UPI. After successful payment, temporary firecracker shop licenses will be automatically generated, which can be downloaded, the Director General said.

“There is no need for physical visits to the fire stations and the entire process is automated, hassle-free and transparent. Traders can apply for cracker shop licenses for two more days for the Diwali festival,” Mr. Ramana said.
“We request the traders to sell crackers in licensed shops only by following all safety precautions,” he added.

Traders are requested to obtain licenses online till the festival day and sell crackers in licensed shops only by following safety precautions, says Fire Services DG Venkata Ramana

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response and Fire Services Department issued temporary licenses for 4,226 firecracker shops in the State for the Diwali festival.

As many as 4,307 traders applied for temporary licenses for selling crackers, of which licenses were issued for 4,226 shops (up to November 6). The highest number of 459 traders applied for licenses online from the East Godavari district, followed by Kakinada (365), Krishna (350), Konaseema (317) and 310 applied for licenses for setting up firecracker shops from the Nellore and Kadapa districts.

Speaking to The Hindu on Friday (November 6, 2026), A.P. State Disaster Response and Fire Services in-charge Director General P. Venkata Ramana said that traders can apply for licenses through Whatsapp No.9441236448. Applicants are requested to call State Fire Control Room No. 9100108101 or 7993987418 for any assistance.

This year, the Fire Services Department has introduced an online system and simplified the process for issuing licenses to firecracker traders in the State, said Mr. Ramana.

People purchase firecrackers at a shop in Bhavani Puram in Vijayawada. | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao

Traders can apply for temporary licenses to Whatsapp No.9441236448. Applicants are requested to submit the name, full address where the cracker shop is proposed to set up, name of district and mandal, nearest fire station and mobile number.

Later, the trader will get a Whatsapp message in which a payment link will be given. The applicant should pay ₹500 through QR Code or UPI. After successful payment, temporary firecracker shop licenses will be automatically generated, which can be downloaded, the Director General said.

“There is no need for physical visits to the fire stations and the entire process is automated, hassle-free and transparent. Traders can apply for cracker shop licenses for two more days for the Diwali festival,” Mr. Ramana said.

“We request the traders to sell crackers in licensed shops only by following all safety precautions,” he added.

articles.title: Nashra Naim elected first woman vice-president of AMU students’ union in 105-year history
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Women candidates won six of the 13 posts, a record five of the 10 cabinet member posts, in the first elections after an eight-year gap

Women candidates created history in the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) Students’ Union (AMUSU) elections, winning six of the 13 posts, including vice-president, the results of which were announced on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Nashra Naim became the first woman to be elected vice-president of the students’ union in the 105-year history of the institution. She secured 7,091 votes, defeating her nearest rival, who polled 5,818 votes, according to the result details.
Women candidates also won a record five of the 10 cabinet member posts, marking a significant increase in their representation in the students’ union.
The post of president was won by Mohammad Noman Ashraf, who secured victory by a margin of more than 4,100 votes, while Mohammad Hamdan was elected secretary, the results showed.

The results were declared by Prof. Javaid Talib, Chief Election Officer for the AMUSU and AMU Court elections, and Prof. Nazia Hasan, Chief Election Officer for the Women’s College Students’ Union elections.
This year’s elections were significant, as they were held after an unprecedented gap of eight years, following persistent protests by students over the past three years.
A senior faculty member said the ongoing Gen Z protests had also influenced the elections.

“Unlike previous years, when campus-specific issues dominated the campaign, this time the discourse also revolved around broader national issues, including those concerning Muslims,” the faculty member said, wishing not to be named.

AMU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Naima Khatoon hailed the “peaceful conduct of the elections,” describing it as “a triumph of the highest democratic traditions” of the institution. She also welcomed the growing participation and representation of women, highlighting the importance of women’s empowerment.
No incident of violence was reported during the election campaign, according to university officials.

articles.title: Suriya’s ‘Scene’: What’s the hype surrounding this Tamil Deepavali release?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil cinema’s Deepavali spotlight falls on Suriya’s ‘Scene,’ a quirky investigative drama directed by Jithu Madhavan that is releasing this weekend in theatres

Scene is the scene this Deepavali in Tamil Nadu. Tamil star Suriya ’s upcoming film, Scene , directed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, has single-handedly taken on the Ramayana storm down South, becoming one of the most anticipated releases this Deepavali weekend.
But what is the whole hype surrounding this Deepavali release all about?

The biggest expectation for the film is whether it will become a hat-trick of hits for Suriya at the box office in 2026. With Karuppu , Suriya became a saving grace for Tamil cinema during a devastatingly poor first half of the year, while Vishwanath & Sons offered a refreshing detour from the gore- and action-heavy films we have been getting from the industry's top stars. And now, with Scene , Suriya might just as well claim the throne as one of the few modern-day stars to deliver three hits in a calendar year. Additionally, Scene is also set to feature Suriya as a cop. And we all know what happens when Suriya takes charge. All hail ‘The One’.

It’s been 12 years since Nazriya Nazim last appeared on the big screen in Tamil cinema. After 2013’s Raja Rani , Nazriya was one of the most promising young female leads in Tamil cinema, and everyone expected her to make big moves to the top. However, after her wedding in 2014 to Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil, Nazriya took a long hiatus from Tamil cinema, with Thirumanam Enum Nikkah as her last release. Even in Malayalam, the actor has been quite choosy with her roles, though her scene-stealing turn in the Telugu film Ante Sundaraniki came as a sweet surprise for fans. And now, with Scene , Nazriya is eyeing a comeback to Tamil cinema.

The craze young Tamil women have for Naslen has to be studied. Since 2024’s Premalu , Naslen has enjoyed a tremendous following across southern states, and with Scene , the Mollywood Times star is finally making his Tamil debut. However, that’s not particularly why Naslen fans might turn up to the theatres this Deepavali. With Scene , Naslen is shedding his chocolate-boy image by playing a serial killer, in what might be one of the first negative roles of his career. Talk about making an entrance!

No, we are not talking about the song from Theri . One of the key highlights of Scene is that it is helmed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, a filmmaker whose previous two films, Romancham and Aavesham , got tremendous reception in Tamil Nadu. Jithu’s knack for humour and the hangover of watching Fahadh play the quirky gangster Ranga are enough promotion for Scene .

Open any ticketing platform on your device, and you will see a surprise. Yes, the early morning shows are back in Tamil Nadu. Scene will be one of the first films to enjoy six shows a day. This comes after the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly-released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release. This is the news cinema fans who know the allure of the early morning shows had been waiting for. It’s going to be a Scene festival at the theatres.

Content creator ‘Lungiboys’ Rajpriyan has played a pivotal role in Scene , while YouTuber Dravid Selvam of Parithabangal fame has penned the dialogues. If you have seen their sketches on social media, you know what to expect.

From the trailer, Scene seems to be a rather quirky investigative drama. Jithu’s frequent collaborator, music composer Sushin Shyam, is making his Tamil debut with Scene . Vineeth Augustian is the cinematographer, Ashwini Kale is the production designer, and Ajmal Sabu is the editor. Chethan D’Souza serves as the stunt choreographer. Suriya and Jyotika produce Scene under their Zhagaram Studios and 2D Entertainment banners.

After 2013’s Raja Rani , Nazriya was one of the most promising young female leads in Tamil cinema, and everyone expected her to make big moves to the top. However, after her wedding in 2014 to Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil, Nazriya took a long hiatus from Tamil cinema, with Thirumanam Enum Nikkah as her last release. Even in Malayalam, the actor has been quite choosy with her roles, though her scene-stealing turn in the Telugu film Ante Sundaraniki came as a sweet surprise for fans. And now, with Scene , Nazriya is eyeing a comeback to Tamil cinema.

The craze young Tamil women have for Naslen has to be studied. Since 2024’s Premalu , Naslen has enjoyed a tremendous following across southern states, and with Scene , the Mollywood Times star is finally making his Tamil debut. However, that’s not particularly why Naslen fans might turn up to the theatres this Deepavali. With Scene , Naslen is shedding his chocolate-boy image by playing a serial killer, in what might be one of the first negative roles of his career. Talk about making an entrance!

No, we are not talking about the song from Theri . One of the key highlights of Scene is that it is helmed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, a filmmaker whose previous two films, Romancham and Aavesham , got tremendous reception in Tamil Nadu. Jithu’s knack for humour and the hangover of watching Fahadh play the quirky gangster Ranga are enough promotion for Scene .

Open any ticketing platform on your device, and you will see a surprise. Yes, the early morning shows are back in Tamil Nadu. Scene will be one of the first films to enjoy six shows a day. This comes after the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly-released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release. This is the news cinema fans who know the allure of the early morning shows had been waiting for. It’s going to be a Scene festival at the theatres.

Content creator ‘Lungiboys’ Rajpriyan has played a pivotal role in Scene , while YouTuber Dravid Selvam of Parithabangal fame has penned the dialogues. If you have seen their sketches on social media, you know what to expect.

From the trailer, Scene seems to be a rather quirky investigative drama. Jithu’s frequent collaborator, music composer Sushin Shyam, is making his Tamil debut with Scene . Vineeth Augustian is the cinematographer, Ashwini Kale is the production designer, and Ajmal Sabu is the editor. Chethan D’Souza serves as the stunt choreographer. Suriya and Jyotika produce Scene under their Zhagaram Studios and 2D Entertainment banners.

articles.title: TDP accuses Chevireddy of ‘rigging’ in Parishad polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: YSRCP alleges 'ragging' by ruling Alliance leaders at polling stations

Alleging various illegal activities by YSRCP leaders during ZPTC/MPTC elections, Chandragiri MLA Pulivarthi Nani and TUDA Chairman C. (Dollars) Divakar Reddy staged a protest near a polling station in Tiruchanur, Tirupati, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) evening.

The two TDP leaders demanded that the State Election Commission (SEC) conduct repolling across all polling stations in Tirupati Rural Mandal, where YSRCP leader Chevireddy Bhaskar Reddy has allegedly committed rigging of votes.

The MLA lashed out strongly against the irregularities, acts of violence, and instances of rigging that reportedly took place during the elections in the mandal. He condemned the deliberate disruption of the electoral process at polling stations — actions intended to incite fear and panic — stating that such behaviour makes a mockery of democracy.

Mr. Divakar Reddy warned the YSRCP leaders that rigging risks distorting the public mandate. He also urged the SEC to respond immediately, investigate the irregularities, and conduct a re-poll in the mandal.
Earlier, Mr. Nani's wife Pulivarthi Sudha Reddy also warned Mr. Bhaskar Reddy that she would follow him wherever he goes to prevent his alleged 'illegal' activities during the Parishad elections.

Meanwhile, Mr. Chevireddy accused the TDP leaders, including the family members of the MLA, of ragging the YSRCP cadre during the Parishad elections. He claimed that the YSRCP activists were not allowed to stay near the polling stations.

fullParagraphs: Under the Modi Government, the common person’s life had become trapped in a dual vicious cycle of inflation and debt, Jairam Ramesh shared on X

The Congress on Friday (November 6, 2026) alleged that the common people have become trapped in a vicious cycle of inflation and debt, and said it was now the responsibility of voters in Punjab, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Goa and Manipur to express their outrage against rising prices by decisively defeating the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared on X a media report which claimed that despite Government assistance under schemes such as the 'PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana', rising inflation in rural areas was placing an increasing financial burden on people.
The report cited a NABARD survey to claim that rural households were spending 53.5% of their total monthly income on food and beverages alone due to inflation.
In his post in Hindi, Mr. Ramesh said that under the Modi Government, the common person's life had become trapped in a dual vicious cycle of inflation and debt.

"The Modi Government's claims of rural prosperity are being exposed by surveys conducted by its own institution, NABARD. More than half of the expenditure of rural households is going towards food. Savings are shrinking, the number of people taking on debt is rising, and for informal loans, people are forced to pay annual interest rates as high as 18.3%," Mr. Ramesh said.
The Government, however, refuses to acknowledge the ground reality, leaving no room for improvement, he said.

"Persistent inflation is breaking the back of the poor and the middle class. The public is already reeling under the burden of rising prices of daily essentials, including vegetables, fruits, pulses, cooking oil, milk and flour," Mr. Ramesh claimed, adding that medical expenses were projected to rise by 10% by 2027.
Prices of items such as soap, biscuits, noodles and other daily necessities were also set to increase after Deepavali, he further claimed.
There was no relief in earnings, no check on inflation and no respite in healthcare costs, Mr. Ramesh said.
The truth about the Modi Government's "development" was that the common person's plate was shrinking, pockets were emptying and the burden of debt was growing heavier, he said.

articles.title: IISc distinguished alumnus/alumna awards for 2026 announced
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) has announced that eight scientists and engineers have been selected for its distinguished alumnus/alumna awards and young alumnus/alumna medals for 2026.
It said the awards recognise alumni who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, society and the institute.
The nominations were assessed by a committee headed by IISc director Govindan Rangarajan.

“The distinguished alumnus/alumna awards and young alumnus/alumna medals are an opportunity to celebrate their journeys and achievements, and to recognise the many ways in which they continue to inspire our community,” Prof. Rangarajan said.
This year’s distinguished alumnus/alumna award recipients are B.S. Manjunath, Dipakar Das Sarma, Jagannath Nayak, Maruthi R. Akella and Rajat Moona.

Mr. Manjunath is a globally recognised computer scientist and academic leader, and the Frank Koenig Distinguished Chair in Signals and Systems and Distinguished Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, U.S.

Mr. Sarma is an internationally renowned condensed matter physicist and materials chemist, currently the ANRF National Science Chair and Emeritus Professor at the Solid State and Structural Chemistry Unit, IISc.
Mr. Nayak is a distinguished defence scientist and Director-General of Missiles and Strategic Systems at DRDO.
Mr. Akella is a globally renowned aerospace scientist and control systems engineer, who currently holds the Cockrell Family Chair in Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin, U.S.
Mr. Moona is an internationally renowned computer scientist and technologist, and Director of IIT Gandhinagar.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: It said the awards recognise alumni who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, society and the institute.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Moona is an internationally renowned computer scientist and technologist, and Director of IIT Gandhinagar.

articles.title: T.N. govt. disbands High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Its mandate has been transferred to the State Law Commission, according to a Government Order issued on November 6, 2026

The High-Level Committee on Union–State Relations, constituted during the erstwhile DMK regime in Tamil Nadu, has been disbanded, and its mandate transferred to the State Law Commission, according to a Government Order (G.O.) issued on November 6, 2026.

In April 2025, then Chief Minister M.K. Stalin had announced in the Legislative Assembly the formation of a three-member high-level panel to review constitutional provisions, statutes, and policies concerning Centre–State relations, and to recommend measures to strengthen federalism and state autonomy.

The committee was chaired by retired Supreme Court Judge Justice Kurian Joseph, with retired IAS officer K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty and former State Planning Commission Vice-Chairman M. Naganathan serving as members. The committee submitted a highly acclaimed Part I of its report to then Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on February 16.
However, the TVK-led government has now chosen to dissolve the committee.

“The Tamil Nadu State Law Commission was re-constituted on 07.08.2026 and is entrusted among others with the broad mandate to examine and make recommendations on matters relating to Inter-State and Centre-State relations along with other subjects, review of the existing laws and improving the legal and institutional frame work of the State,” the G.O pointed out.

The G.O. said, “The High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations is a ‘non-statutory body’, examining various issues relating to Union-State relations, has a considerable similarity and overlap in the nature and scope of the functions entrusted to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission. Therefore, after careful consideration, the Government have decided to discontinue the services of the High-Level Committee with immediate effect.”

While the G.O. stresses that the Committee was a “not-statutory body”, the State Law Commission, which will now take up the task, is also not a statutory body. It is an executive body created by a Government Order.

articles.title: Court acquits DMK leader Ponmudy in ‘derogatory’ religious remarks case after complainant withdraws petition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A BJP councillor filed a complaint alleging that Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

A Metropolitan Magistrate court has acquitted former Tamil Nadu Minister and DMK leader K. Ponmudy of charges related to alleged derogatory remarks concerning Shaivism and Vaishnavism, following the complainant’s withdrawal of her private petition after Ponmudy issued a public apology.

The III Metropolitan Magistrate, George Town, C. Sundarapandian, pronounced the judgment on September 23, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against Mr. Ponmudy beyond reasonable doubt.

The case arose from a speech Mr. Ponmudy gave on April 6, 2025, at Anbagam, the DMK Youth Wing headquarters on Anna Salai, Teynampet, during a centenary celebration of party member Thiruvarur Thangaraj.

At the event, Mr. Ponmudy allegedly compared the religious symbols worn by Shaivites and Vaishnavites to sexual positions while narrating an anecdote involving a sex worker. The speech was uploaded on the YouTube channel Neerthirai and circulated on social media platforms.
Following public outrage, the DMK stripped Mr. Ponmudy of his party post as deputy general secretary. He later resigned as Minister.

Uma Anandan, a BJP councillor, filed a complaint alleging the remarks deliberately insulted Hindu beliefs and hurt religious sentiments. She alleged Mr. Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

Since the Nungambakkam Police did not take any action, she filed a private complaint before the XVIII Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Saidapet, on June 12, 2025. The complaint was subsequently transferred to the special court designated to try cases involving elected MPs and MLAs, and later to the III Metropolitan Magistrate Court, George Town, following changes in the court’s jurisdiction.

During the proceedings, Mr. Ponmudy pleaded not guilty and sought trial. His counsel argued that the ingredients required to establish the offences were not made out. There were no two identifiable groups between whom enmity had been promoted to attract Section 196(1)(a), and the allegations did not satisfy the requirements of Sections 299 and 302, the defence submitted. It also contended that prior sanction under Section 217 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) had not been obtained.
However, during her examination, Ms. Anandan submitted a petition seeking withdrawal of the complaint along with an affidavit.
In her statement, Ms. Anandan said she decided to withdraw the case after he publicly apologised for his remarks and assured that he would not make such statements in the future.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 06 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Court acquits DMK leader Ponmudy in ‘derogatory’ religious remarks case after complainant withdraws petition

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

A BJP councillor filed a complaint alleging that Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

A Metropolitan Magistrate court has acquitted former Tamil Nadu Minister and DMK leader K. Ponmudy of charges related to alleged derogatory remarks concerning Shaivism and Vaishnavism, following the complainant’s withdrawal of her private petition after Ponmudy issued a public apology.

The III Metropolitan Magistrate, George Town, C. Sundarapandian, pronounced the judgment on September 23, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against Mr. Ponmudy beyond reasonable doubt.

The case arose from a speech Mr. Ponmudy gave on April 6, 2025, at Anbagam, the DMK Youth Wing headquarters on Anna Salai, Teynampet, during a centenary celebration of party member Thiruvarur Thangaraj.

At the event, Mr. Ponmudy allegedly compared the religious symbols worn by Shaivites and Vaishnavites to sexual positions while narrating an anecdote involving a sex worker. The speech was uploaded on the YouTube channel Neerthirai and circulated on social media platforms.

Following public outrage, the DMK stripped Mr. Ponmudy of his party post as deputy general secretary. He later resigned as Minister.

Uma Anandan, a BJP councillor, filed a complaint alleging the remarks deliberately insulted Hindu beliefs and hurt religious sentiments. She alleged Mr. Ponmudy’s speech promoted hatred and ill-will towards the Hindu religion.

Since the Nungambakkam Police did not take any action, she filed a private complaint before the XVIII Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Saidapet, on June 12, 2025. The complaint was subsequently transferred to the special court designated to try cases involving elected MPs and MLAs, and later to the III Metropolitan Magistrate Court, George Town, following changes in the court’s jurisdiction.

During the proceedings, Mr. Ponmudy pleaded not guilty and sought trial. His counsel argued that the ingredients required to establish the offences were not made out. There were no two identifiable groups between whom enmity had been promoted to attract Section 196(1)(a), and the allegations did not satisfy the requirements of Sections 299 and 302, the defence submitted. It also contended that prior sanction under Section 217 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) had not been obtained.

However, during her examination, Ms. Anandan submitted a petition seeking withdrawal of the complaint along with an affidavit.

In her statement, Ms. Anandan said she decided to withdraw the case after he publicly apologised for his remarks and assured that he would not make such statements in the future.

articles.title: Protest suspended, not withdrawn, say KRRS leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sugarcane farmers in Belagavi claimed to have only suspended their agitation and not withdrawn it completely.
“Our protest will continue till the farmers take home a total of ₹5,500 per tonne,’’ Chunappa Pujeri, Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene president, told reporters in Gurlapur on Friday.

“We have accepted the price of ₹3,600 per tonne offered by factories as a temporary solution to our problems. This is conditional to the fact that the factories have agreed to share their profits with us. This is the first time in the country that the factories have agreed to a profit-sharing formula,” Mr. Pujeri said.

“However, our demand for ₹5,500 per tonne remains unchanged. We also expect Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to release an incentive of ₹1,000 per tonne as State Advised Price. The State government in neighbouring Maharashtra has promised to release ₹3,900 in the first instalment, ₹100 later and ₹200 if the Union government revises the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar. The Tamil Nadu government is releasing an SAP of ₹700 per tonne, in addition to the centrally mandated Fair and Remunerative Price. The governments in UP and Haryana are also offering incentives. Karnataka should do so to,” he said.

Meanwhile, farmers in Vijayapura demanded that the profit-sharing formula agreed upon in Belagavi be implemented across the State. KRRS leaders submitted a memorandum to the Deputy Commissioner K. Anand. He responded by saying that he would convene a meeting of all factories and farmers’ leaders in Vijayapura on Saturday.

“There are 10 sugar factories in the district, but all of them are not paying the same price. Last year, while the factories in the Krishna river belt paid around ₹3,300 per tonne, those in the Bhima river belt paid only around ₹3,000. This year, we want all the factories to pay ₹3,600 per tonne,” said Shantagouda Patil, KRRS leader. Sangamesh Sagar, Ramanagouda Patil, Dayananda Koli, Mahadeva Banasode, Sangappa Takke, Abhishekha Hoogar, Mudakanna and other leaders were present.

In Bagalkot, however, farmers leaders refused to accept the price of ₹3,600 offered by factories. “We have seen before our own eyes that a politician who was a director in one cooperative factory has now set up 20 private factories. It shows that they are regularly making profits. If they want to make unlimited money, why should the farmers suffer? We want ₹5,500 per tonne for sugarcane,” they alleged.

Meanwhile, Raju Shetti, former MP and founder of the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatan (SSS), ended his national highway rasta roko protest on Friday. He announced that the State government had announced that the farmers were likely to get ₹4,200 in three installments. The factories will first pay ₹3,900 per tonne before crushing, ₹100 after the end of crushing and ₹200 per tonne if the Union government revises MSP for sugar. This was announced after a meeting of factories and farmers convened by Minister Hassan Mushrif, Mr. Shetti said.
He gave the credit to the united struggle of Karnataka and Maharashtra for what he called was an interim success of the agitation.
The SSS members had blocked the Pune-Bangalore highway at Kini zakat naka for two days. It was opened by Friday evening.

articles.title: ADNOC inks 10-year LNG supply and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday signed a 10-year sales and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2028, further strengthening its presence in India’s expanding gas market.
The agreement marks ADNOC’s fifth LNG supply deal with an Indian company, following similar arrangements with Bharat Petroleum, Indian Oil Corporation, GAIL and Hindustan Petroleum.
Under the agreement, XRG, ADNOC’s international investment arm, will supply LNG produced outside the Gulf and owned by it through ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform.

Rashid Al Mazrouei, Chief Marketing & Origination Officer (LNG) at ADNOC, said, “It represents the first sale of molecules from XRG’s international portfolio, reinforcing our commitment to delivering reliable, long-term LNG supplies.”

He added, “Through our integrated LNG marketing and trading platform, we are connecting our growing international portfolio with customers in key regions across global markets, while providing India with reliable, flexible and long-term LNG supplies.”

ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform also has supply agreements with Japan’s INPEX and Thailand’s Gulf Group. The platform aims to market 47 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG beyond 2030.
Avantika Singh Aulakh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, said, “Through this partnership, Gujarat Energy and ADNOC are joining forces to fully realize the power of our collaboration.”
Gujarat Energy operates a city gas distribution network spanning 44 districts across six states.

This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday signed a 10-year sales and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2028, further strengthening its presence in India’s expanding gas market.

The agreement marks ADNOC’s fifth LNG supply deal with an Indian company, following similar arrangements with Bharat Petroleum, Indian Oil Corporation, GAIL and Hindustan Petroleum.

Under the agreement, XRG, ADNOC’s international investment arm, will supply LNG produced outside the Gulf and owned by it through ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform.

Rashid Al Mazrouei, Chief Marketing & Origination Officer (LNG) at ADNOC, said, “It represents the first sale of molecules from XRG’s international portfolio, reinforcing our commitment to delivering reliable, long-term LNG supplies.”

He added, “Through our integrated LNG marketing and trading platform, we are connecting our growing international portfolio with customers in key regions across global markets, while providing India with reliable, flexible and long-term LNG supplies.”

ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform also has supply agreements with Japan’s INPEX and Thailand’s Gulf Group. The platform aims to market 47 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG beyond 2030.

Avantika Singh Aulakh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, said, “Through this partnership, Gujarat Energy and ADNOC are joining forces to fully realize the power of our collaboration.”

Gujarat Energy operates a city gas distribution network spanning 44 districts across six states.

fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 people, including Rohingya refugees, during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers near the Myanmar border, the military said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
One soldier was killed in the clash on Thursday (November 5, 2026) night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

ISPR said that security forces launched an operation in the hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf, close to the border with Myanmar, after receiving a tip-off that an armed gang of 15 to 16 suspected traffickers had abducted around 120 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis.
"During the exchange of fire, an army soldier, Md. Titash Sheikh, was shot. The bullet struck his left shoulder. He was bleeding profusely," the statement said.
Bangladesh hosts more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, most of whom fled a brutal military crackdown in neighbouring Myanmar in 2017.
Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.
The 2017 Myanmar crackdown, which saw Rohingya villages burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case at the UN's top court in The Hague.

articles.title: Iran Guards say two tankers caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media on Friday (November 6, 2026) that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had similar fates.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and escorted tankers through the strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

"Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorised route struck mines," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement carried by state TV.

"The two tankers had deactivated all of their navigation and identification systems and were attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz... with the support of the aggressor and terrorist American military, but following the collision with mines, they caught fire and were brought to a stop," the statement added.
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.
There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.

articles.title: Myanmar to conduct byelections next April
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives

Myanmar will hold byelections next April, the polling commission said on Friday (November 6, 2026), encompassing areas where the pro-military parliament could not previously hold voting due to the country's devastating civil war.
The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives.
Myanmar has been embroiled in civil war since the military ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021.
The junta staged phased elections last December and January, which it touted as a return to democracy following the coup.
But the highly restrictive poll was blocked in areas where rebels seized control in opposition to military rule, rejecting the elections as a charade.
The Union Election Commission said byelections will take place on April 4, 2027 in 39 constituencies of the lower and upper houses of Parliament, according to a statement published by state media.
According to an AFP tally, one-third of those constituencies are places where voting in the previous elections was called off for security reasons.
The scheduled votes are in areas where fighting is still raging, though, including the northern region of Sagaing, central Mandalay region and the western state of Chin.
The remaining two-thirds of constituencies will replace lawmakers who have been compelled by the constitution to vacate their seats after being promoted to senior government roles.
Myanmar's Parliament is dominated by lawmakers from the pro-military Union Solidarity and Development Party, while Suu Kyi's party was dissolved and she remains detained.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts
Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.
The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts

Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.

The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

The overall air quality of Delhi worsened and continued to be in the “very poor” category on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution, according to official data.
Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Faridabad also witnessed overall “very poor” air quality, on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 391 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “severe” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 369 (very poor) on Thursday at 4 p.m. on Thursday, slightly down from 377 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: ACB detects 90 suspicious UPI transactions at LB Nagar fire station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 90 suspicious UPI transactions, ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹4,500 each, were detected on the mobile phones of staff at the LB Nagar Fire Station during a surprise check by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Friday, November 6.

The transactions had taken place during the preceding week amid allegations that fire station personnel were collecting amounts higher than the prescribed fee for issuing temporary firecracker shop licences. The prescribed online fee for a temporary licence is ₹500. The ACB found that nearly 397 applications had been received for such licences, of which 26 were still pending.

The bureau is probing the reasons for the delay in processing the applications and examining the alleged collection of excess amounts. The ACB has appealed to the public to report any demand for money beyond the prescribed fee or unexplained delays in processing applications. Complaints can be made through its toll-free number 1064 or WhatsApp number 9440446106.

Political & National Report: ACB detects 90 suspicious UPI transactions at LB Nagar fire station. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Cyberabad Police explore one-way traffic system across Biodiversity, HITEC City corridors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyberabad Police have initiated steps to explore a one-way traffic system along the Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace and HITEC City corridor to ease congestion during peak hours.

Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh, accompanied by Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh, RTC officials and other traffic police personnel, inspected the proposed route on Friday. The inspection covered Biodiversity Junction, IKEA, T-Works, Qualcomm, Dallas Centre Road and surrounding areas.

The proposed one-way corridor would cover Biodiversity Junction, Mindspace Rotary, Times Square Road, Knowledge City Road, Qualcomm and Dallas Centre Road. Officials examined traffic flow patterns, road conditions and major conflict points along the stretch to assess the feasibility of the proposal and identify measures to reduce congestion.

During the inspection, Mr Ramesh instructed officials to prepare a detailed report covering a comprehensive traffic flow study, identified bottlenecks and conflict points, supported by relevant visuals.

He also directed them to conduct a block-wise assessment of buildings contributing to traffic congestion, including the anticipated traffic impact, vehicle volume generated by each building, availability of parking facilities and parking capacity.
The exercise aims to identify suitable traffic management measures and streamline vehicular movement around T-Hub, IKEA, Knowledge City, Qualcomm and Biodiversity.

fullParagraphs: The four-day Karnataka Rajyotsava Bird Count (KRBC), an initiative by eBird held from October 30 to November 2, recorded 139 bird species, generating 79 checklists with 18 birds participating, highlighting the region’s avian diversity. A major highlight was the sighting of greater flamingos at Bhosga Kere for the first time.

A bird walk on this occasion was organised by local group Winged Endeavours as part of the first State-wide initiative under the eBird platform; the exercise aimed to document Karnataka’s bird diversity, recording 62 species across the city during the birding session.

K.S. Aishwarya of Winged Endeavours led the participants of the bird walk across different locations, including lakes and birding hot spots in the city, introducing them to birdwatching and encouraging them to document local birdlife.

Depletion of food resources in their native habitats prompted birds to move to regions offering better feeding opportunities. Some destinations also served as breeding grounds, improving the survival prospects of their young, she said.

Kalaburagi’s relatively mild winters make it a suitable seasonal habitat for migratory birds escaping severe cold in their native ranges. Winter visitors are generally spotted in the region from October to early March, she added.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s after The Hindu report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Rajasthan police rescue six minors forced into sex work, five arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police acted after taking cognisance of a ‘Ground Zero’ report in August by The Hindu.

The Rajasthan police has rescued six minor girls of the Banchhada community in Jhalawar district and arrested five people – most of whom were related to the girls – for allegedly pushing them into sex work, officers said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Speaking to The Hindu , Jhalawar Superintendent of Police (SP) Amit Kumar said that the girls, aged between 12 and 17, were rescued in raids conducted in the Bhawanimandi area on November 3 and that medical and forensic examinations have confirmed sexual exploitation of five of the girls.

articles.title: Yadgir bandh evokes good response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Yadgir bandh called by various organisations under the leadership of former Minister Narasimha Naik (Rajugouda) evoked a good response across the Yadgir district headquarters, as well as in Shorapur and Hunsagi taluks, on Friday.

​The agitation was staged to demand the uninterrupted release of water from the Basavasagar reservoir through the Narayanpur Left and Right Bank Canals until the end of November to protect standing crops, including paddy, green chili, and cotton.
​Commercial establishments, markets, and shops voluntarily shut down operations until 3 p.m. in solidarity with the farmers. However, public transport remained largely unaffected.
​Hundreds of farmers gathered near the Tahsildar’s office in Yadgir before marching to the Subhash Chandra Bose Circle, where they staged a demonstration for several hours.

​Addressing the rally, Mr. Naik alleged that despite sufficient water storage in the reservoir, discharges were being routed overnight to neighboring Telangana while local agricultural requirements were overlooked. Rebutting district in-charge Minister Sharan Prakash Patil’s denial of the allegations, Mr. Naik claimed that local farmers possessed video evidence documenting the inter-State water transfer.

​He appealed to Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil to allocate at least 14 tmcft of water to Yadgir district to save standing crops, highlighting that 28 tmcft of water had already been reserved for drinking purposes in Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts.

​Mr. Naik also urged Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar to withdraw cases registered against farmers during previous agitations, offering to have himself booked first instead. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigama Limited enforces its proposed Warabandhi shutdown starting November 12.
​The protest garnered support from multiple farmer associations, pro-Kannada outfits, Dalit organisations, and the local Advocates’ Association.

​A formal memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister was submitted through Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve, who assured the protesters that their demands and grievances would be forwarded to higher authorities promptly.
​Basavaraj Veebhutihalli, Rachanagouda Mudnal, Mahesh Reddy Mudnal, Devendra Nath Nad, Lalita Anapur, Mareppa Chattarkar, Mareppa Naik, Bheemu Naik and others were present at the demonstration.

articles.title: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz
Yemen’s Houthis said the toll from an airstrike on a market in Taiz province, southwestern Yemen, on Friday (November 6, 2026) increased to 30 dead, as the warring sides traded blame for the attack.

“Saudi enemy aircraft targeted the Hadara market in Waziyah district, resulting in 30 deaths and eight injuries,” the Houthis’ Health Ministry said in a statement carried by the group’s Saba news agency, updating an earlier toll.
It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz.
He said that the death toll was expected to rise from the airstrikes, which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition.

Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people, without providing details on the actual toll. But the authorities in Taiz blamed the Houthis for the incident. They said that no airstrikes were carried out in the area.
The Associated Press couldn't immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: on India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Trump debacle: on the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan, making him the first Muslim Senator in history; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan, making him the first Muslim Senator in history; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.
